sceneAlt: A cheerful child's bedroom: a bed with a starry duvet, a rocking horse and a guitar on the left, a wardrobe, a shelf with a globe, a rocket and a doll, and a small desk with a lamp and a chair at the back, a play tent, a teddy bear, a toy chest and a chalkboard on the right, and a round rug with a toy train, a picture book, a puzzle and a ball in the middle.
help.hook: A child's bedroom full of toys: tap each thing in the picture, then give it its article.
help.intro: A picture hunt instead of a deck: one cheerful, slightly messy child's bedroom with 32 things to find in it, every one an everyday noun — das Bett, der Kleiderschrank, die Eisenbahn, das Schaukelpferd, the toys on the rug and the kite on the wall. The prompt asks a question like Wo ist der Teppich? and you tap the object in the picture. A tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking; after three misses the right one is shown. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. Once you have passed a run, the hunt gets harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Eisenbahn?), and after the find you pick der, die or das yourself. No object is asked twice in the same run.
help.tips[0].title: Compounds in the bedroom: the last part decides
help.tips[0].text: Many toys here are compounds, and the last part decides the article. Schaukel + Pferd: das Pferd, so das Schaukelpferd. Spielzeug + Kiste: die Kiste, so die Spielzeugkiste. Look at the last word and you have the article.
help.tips[0].check.why: The last part is das Auto, so the whole word is das Spielzeugauto.
help.tips[1].text: Schreibtisch and Schreibtischlampe start the same, but the article follows the end of the word: der Tisch makes der Schreibtisch, die Lampe makes die Schreibtischlampe. The same goes for Spielzeug: das Spielzeugauto, but die Spielzeugkiste.
help.tips[1].check.why: The last part is der Schrank, so it is der Kleiderschrank; die Kleider at the front does not count.
help.tips[2].title: Many words in -e are feminine
help.tips[2].text: Nouns that end in -e are very often die: die Puppe, die Rakete, die Gitarre, die Bettdecke. It is a strong pattern, not a law, but when you have to guess an -e word, guess die.
help.tips[2].check.why: Gitarre ends in -e, and like most -e nouns it is feminine.
help.remember[0]: The last part of a compound sets the article: der Schrank → der Kleiderschrank.
help.remember[1]: Most nouns ending in -e are die: die Puppe, die Rakete, die Gitarre.
help.remember[2]: Der Drachen is the kite on the wall; the plural is die Drachen, unchanged.
